name: Pije
orthography_note: Practical orthography of Haudricourt & Ozanne-Rivierre (1982: 17): h before a consonant marks aspiration (ph, hm, hl), b d j g bw are prenasalised, ny ng = ɲ ŋ, a circumflex marks a nasal vowel, doubled vowels are long. IPA here.
notes: Northern New Caledonian, Hienghène region: Tiendanite, Ouenghip, Tiouandé (Haudricourt & Ozanne-Rivierre 1982: 9-10). With Fwâi and Nemi it keeps old POc dentals before *a as apicals, which Jawe palatalises (§1.2); it has a thematic vowel a in possessed nouns where the others have e (§1.3); the old post-nasalised consonants appear as aspirates followed by nasal vowels (§1.4). Glottocode and coordinates from the language metadata of Ross et al. (2023).

name: Fwâi
orthography_note: As for Pije (Haudricourt & Ozanne-Rivierre 1982: 17-18). IPA here.
notes: Northern New Caledonian: lower Hienghène valley, Tanghène valley and the coast from Pindache to the mouth of the Ouaième; it is replacing Nemi in the villages north of that mouth (Haudricourt & Ozanne-Rivierre 1982: 18). Oral stops and strong continuants occur only in loans (p. 18). Glottocode and coordinates from the language metadata of Ross et al. (2023).

name: Jawe
orthography_note: As for Pije; ch is written c before a nasal vowel; ü and ë are [y] and [œ] (Haudricourt & Ozanne-Rivierre 1982: 21-23). IPA here.
notes: Northern New Caledonian: east coast from Colnett to Tchambouène, the Ouaième valley at Pangou, and the central chain at Ouayaguette (Wevia) and Ouahat. Two varieties: Yambé (Y), whose system is entered here, and Wevia (W), which keeps the post-nasalised consonants of Nemi 2, at least initially; in Yambé they became aspirated stops followed by nasal vowels (Haudricourt & Ozanne-Rivierre 1982: 21). Jawe palatalises old dentals before *a (§1.2). Glottocode and coordinates from the language metadata of Ross et al. (2023).
